newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgium to start talks with Fortis on bank stake.
newsitem.headline: Belgium to start talks with Fortis on bank stake.

text.p: The Belgian cabinet approved a draft law on the sale of about half of the state's equity stake in ASLK/CGER Bank and ALSK/CGER Insurance on Friday.
It said in a statement the approval cleared the way for talks with ASLK/CGER's private sector shareholder, the Fortis group, with a view to the transfer of the state's 24.7 percent stake.
The state's FPM/SFP Federal Participation Company currently holds 49.9 percent of ASLK. After the sale it wil have 25.1 percent, the minimum required by Belgian law.
Fortis acquired a 49.9 percent stake in ASLK late in 1993. ASLK Bank and ASLK Insurance each hold 0.1 percent of the group's shares.
The cabinet's decision marks the formal start of negotiations.
In March Paul Van Rompuy, director of FPM/SFP, said both sides were awaiting suggestions from the state privatisation committee about how the sale could be realised.
Friday's cabinet statement indicated the government had ruled out a bourse listing for ASLK and went against a professed preference by Finance Minister Philippe Maystadt for a listing.

Maystadt had favoured a listing because it would give the government a reference framework for the price, because otherwise ASLK would be the only one of the five major banks not be listed and, finally, because it would be "a good operation" for Brussels as a financial centre.
A Finance Ministry spokeswoman had no comment on the cabinet decision or on Maystadt's current position on the issue.
Fortis paid 35 billion francs for its initial 49 percent stake in ASLK.
